title: Job cards
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y6 lesson 5 (Job cards (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 5: Earning money. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

model.title: Hassan earns £12 an hour and works 30 hours. Weekly pay?

cards: Selling fruit at a fair price
Hiding faults when selling a car
blocks.title: Sort into: Halal / Not halal
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Halal, Not halal.
blocks.answer: Halal: Selling fruit at a fair price; Teaching; Repairing phones. Not halal: Selling alcohol; Hiding faults when selling a car; Earning interest on loans

cards:
Baker
£11.50 an hour
20 hours a week

Delivery driver
£12.00 an hour
35 hours a week

Teaching assistant
£12.50 an hour
30 hours a week

Phone repairer
£14.00 an hour
25 hours a week
blocks.task: work out the weekly pay for each job (pay = hours x rate).

blocks.answers: Baker: 20 x £11.50 = £230; Delivery driver: 35 x £12.00 = £420; Teaching assistant: 30 x £12.50 = £375; Phone repairer: 25 x £14.00 = £350 (before deductions).

keywords.def: money paid for work, often per hour
a fixed amount paid each year, usually monthly
money earned in a way Islam allows (حَلَال)

questions.q: Why might a surgeon earn more than a shop assistant?
questions.a: Years of training and specialist skills.

questions.q: Core: Job cards (pupil PDF): work out weekly pay for four jobs.
Extend: Choose a job you might like. Write the skills and training it needs.
Stretch: Explain why earning from haram sources is not allowed even if it pays more.
questions.a: Islam values honest, halal provision over profit; haram earnings harm others and bring no barakah.

questions.q: A salary is... A) paid per hour B) a fixed yearly amount paid monthly C) a gift
questions.a: B) a fixed yearly amount paid monthly
options: A fixed yearly amount paid monthly

questions.q: Big question: is all money equally good? Why?
questions.a: No: only halal, honest earnings are good.
